page: Amazon Web Services r5dn.2xlarge is a memory-optimized instance built on the Nitro hypervisor. It features an x86_64 architecture powered by an Intel Xeon 8259CL processor operating at 3.1 GHz. The configuration includes 8 vCPUs, which correspond to 4 physical cores with 2 threads per core under a dedicated CPU allocation. The system is equipped with 64.0 GB of DDR4 memory running at 3 GHz, yielding 8.0 GB of RAM per core, and features a 35 MB L3 cache with support for AVX-512 vector extensions.

This instance includes 300 GB of local NVMe SSD storage and is network and EBS optimized. It provides a baseline network bandwidth of 8 Gbps. No complimentary public IPv4 addresses are included with this instance type.

Benchmark data indicates average performance across several categories, including stress-ng multi-core CPU performance, PassMark CPU score, and memory bandwidth tests. However, single-core performance is weak, as shown by stress-ng single-core and gzip compression benchmarks. Multi-threaded bzip3 decompression and Geekbench multi-core scores also fall into the weak category. LLM inference speeds are weak to poor, with the 7B model achieving 10.04 tokens per second for prompt processing and 6.2 tokens per second for text generation.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the r5dn.2xlarge offers a high memory-to-vCPU ratio combined with local NVMe storage, making it suitable for memory-intensive workloads that require fast local scratch space. Tradeoffs include lower single-core compute efficiency and weak database operation scores in PassMark. Appropriate workloads include memory-intensive applications, caching layers, and workloads requiring moderate network throughput and local NVMe storage.
